sentences.text:
1
 The Honourable Sri Justice E. V. Venugopal
 Criminal Petition No.2291 Of 2014
O R D E R:

The present Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. seeking to quash the proceedings in Crime No.18 of 2014 registered against the petitioners/accused for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 468, 471, 447 and 506 IPC on the file of Station House Officer, Kandukur Police Station, Cyberabad, Ranga Reddy District.

2. Heard Mr. Ashok Raj, learned counsel for the petitioners, Mr. Vizarath Ali, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent State and Mr. J. Kanakaiah, learned counsel for respondent Nos.2 and 3.
3.

The brief facts of the case are that respondent No.3-de facto complainant, claiming himself to be the General Power of Attorney of M/s. Musaddilal Constructions & Real Estates (P)
Limited-respondent No.2 company, lodged a complaint before the Station House Officer, Kandukur Police Station, Cyberabad, Ranga Reddy District, on 01.02.2014, against petitioners-accused No.1 to 3 alleging that respondent No.3 on behalf of respondent No.2 company, entered an agreement of sale with one Smt. Lakshmi Mansukhani, wife of T.G. Mansukani, resident of Hyderabad vide document No.22064/2006 dated 06.11.2006 for purchase of lands admeasuring Acs.11.18 guntas situated in Survey Nos.458, 474 and 477 at Lemoor Village, Kandukur Mandal, Ranga Reddy District.

Later, on verification, it came to be known that some documents in respect of the above said land were executed in favour of M/s. Harish Teak Plantation Private Limited and that petitioner No.1 by impersonating petitioner No.2 with the active connivance of her father and some persons, got fabricated the documents in the form of registered sale deeds vide document Nos.4268/1998 and 4269/1998 and that as on the date of the alleged sale deeds, the vendor of the de facto complainant was the absolute owner and possessor of the land and that with an intention to have wrongful gain to them, the petitioners have fabricated the documents though as on the date of execution of sale deeds in favour of M/s. Harish Teak Plantation Private Limited and petitioner No.1 the said Krishnaveni was not having right, title and interest over the land.
He further alleged that while the matter stood thus, on 28.01.2014, the petitioners trespassed into their land and threatened the inmates with dire consequences.
In the circumstances, respondent No.3 lodged a complaint before the Station House Officer, Kandukur Police Station, Cyberabad, against the petitioners.

Thereupon, the police registered a case in Crime No.18 of 2014 against the petitioners for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 468, 471, 447 and 506 I.P.C.

4. Respondent Nos.2 and 3 filed a counter affidavit stating that in respect of the schedule property,
mutation proceedings issued in favour of the petitioners were set aside by the appellate authority and the same was confirmed by the revisional authority.
In view of the same, the petitioners trespassed into the schedule property and threatened the inmates with dire consequences.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioners/accused submits that respondent No.3/de facto complainant filed O.S.No.461 of 2011 in the Court of learned III Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B. Nagar, against petitioner Nos.1 and 2 for declaration of title over the said land and to declare the registered sale deeds No.4248 and 4249 of 1998 dated 23.12.1998 as null and void and to handover the physical possession of the schedule property.

entities.text: III Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B. Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: From this, it is clear that respondent Nos.2 and 3 are not in possession of the schedule property.
Therefore, the question of the petitioners trespassing into the schedule property does not arise.
He further submits that in A.S.No.390 of 2019, the Division Bench of this Court vide order dated 31.07.2019 granted status quo with regard to the possession over the schedule property.

In support of the same, he relied on the decisions of the Apex Court in Prof. R. K. Vijayasarathy and another Vs. Sudha Seetharam and another 1 and Mitesh Kumar J. Sha Vs. State of Karnataka and Others 2 and the decision of the Madras High Court in Muthammal; P Esakkiammal @ Devi; P Ramalakshmi; P Rajangam Pillai; P. Parameswaran; P.
Ganapathy Pillai; P. Sundararajan; P. Velappan Vs. S. Thangam.

entities.text: Prof. R. K. Vijayasarathy and another Vs. Sudha Seetharam and another 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Mitesh Kumar J. Sha Vs. State of Karnataka and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, he prays for quashing the proceedings in Crime No.18 of 2014 on the file of Kandukur Police Station, Cyberabad, Ranga Reddy District.

6. Learned counsel for respondent Nos.2 and 3 contended that O.S.No.461 of 2011 filed by respondent No.2 was decreed in their favour which would clearly show that respondent No.2 has got title over the schedule property and that though the Division Bench of this Court granted status quo in respect of the schedule property in A.S.No.390 of 2019, the said order does not confer 1 (2019) 16 Supreme Court Cases 739 2 AIR 2021 Supreme Court 5298 any right or title upon the petitioners and therefore, he seeks to dismiss the Criminal Petition.
7.
Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor would submit that by virtue of interim stay granted by this Court, the investigation process has been stalled.
Unless and until the investigation is proceeded with further and unless the truth comes out, the impugned proceedings against the petitioners cannot be quashed.
Therefore, he seeks to pass appropriate orders.

8. In view of aforesaid submissions and inasmuch as the investigation is not yet completed in the subject crime, without going into the merits of the matter, this Court is of the opinion that the respondent police shall keep in mind all the aspects narrated above and also the decisions cited (supra 1, 2, 3 and 4) and complete the investigation strictly in accordance with law.

Further, as the imprisonment prescribed for the alleged offences is less than seven years, the respondent police shall follow the procedure as contemplated under Section 41-A of Cr.P.C. and the guidelines formulated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar 3 scrupulously.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is needless to mention that any deviation in this regard will be viewed seriously.

9. With the above direction, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.
